newsitem.title: ESTONIA: POHJOLA TO MERGE SALAMA AROUND SUMMER.
newsitem.headline: POHJOLA TO MERGE SALAMA AROUND SUMMER.

text.p: Finnish insurer Pohjola said on Thursday it still planned to consolidate life-insurer Salama into its group structure around summer.
"It (the consolidation of Salama) is expected to happen around summer...but no final decision has been made yet," Pohjola vice president, Jyrki Hagglund told Reuters.

Pohjola announced in January the plan to take over Salama from its associate mutual Suomi, aiming to consolidate it from July 1, but the transfer was delayed in March. Acccording to he plan, Suomi would stop selling life insurance.
Suomi's board of trustees is due to decide on the plan on April 29 and its representatives on May 6, Pohjola has said.

"The reason to take Salama into a stock exchange listed group is to secure future capital needs," Hagglund said. "The life-insurance market is going to grow very fast during the next five years in Finland and it needs some extra capital."
Consolidation will not have a big impact on Pohjola's profit figures and the main idea is to get resources for the life-insurer, he added.
